themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 82 THIS WEEK versus 19.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (320% increase, z-score: 5.78)—a sharp acceleration suggesting widespread pavement, pothole, or infrastructure failures demanding urgent investigation into root cause and repair backlog.
evidence: 82 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 19.5 weekly baseline (320% spike)
Z-score of 5.78 indicates extremely rare statistical deviation
532 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (85 new buildings, 12 demolitions) may indicate construction-related street damage
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent construction activity (DOB permits) is damaging streets faster than repairs can occur
Document resident impact: commute delays, vehicle damage, accessibility issues for elderly/disabled residents

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints surged to 21 THIS WEEK from 7.6 weekly average (175% increase, z-score: 6.15)—the second-largest spike after street conditions—indicating a sudden environmental disturbance affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 21 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.6 weekly average (175% increase)
Noise ranks 5th in 90-day volume (1,259 total) but sudden spike suggests acute new problem, not chronic baseline
reporting_angles: Identify source: construction sites, nightlife venue, new industrial activity, or transit disruption?
Survey residents on frequency, timing, and whether noise correlates with recent development projects (3 active rezonings underway)

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Vandalism Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 12 THIS WEEK from 2.5 weekly average (380% increase, z-score: 4.91)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or deterioration in neighborhood maintenance that warrants swift inspection and community engagement.
evidence: 12 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly baseline (380% spike)
Concurrent spike in dirty condition complaints (74 2 weeks ago vs. 19.1 avg, 287% increase) suggests neighborhood sanitation breakdown
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations: is graffiti clustered (specific corridor/business district) or dispersed?
Interview NYPD Precinct about gang activity, trespassing arrests, or transit hub vandalism; check if related to three active rezoning projects drawing unwanted attention

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Reports Quadruple
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 12 TWO WEEKS AGO from 2.4 weekly average (405% increase, z-score: 7.9)—the highest z-score in dataset—indicating potential disease vector, pest infestation, or environmental hazard requiring urgent public health assessment.
evidence: 12 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (405% spike)
Highest z-score in entire dataset (7.9), indicating rarest/most severe statistical anomaly
Concurrent spike in dirty condition (287% increase) and indoor air quality complaints (195% increase) suggests potential environmental health cascade
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and Department of Health: are there disease outbreaks (rabies, avian flu, rat-borne illness) being tracked in Sheepshead Bay/Gravesend?
Investigate whether waterfront conditions (Sheepshead Bay is coastal) are contributing—algal bloom, polluted water driving dead wildlife ashore?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints rose to 7 LAST WEEK from 2.4 weekly average (195% increase, z-score: 4.16)—a health signal potentially linked to heating system failures (heat/hot water is #2 complaint type at 2,151 total), mold, or poor ventilation in aging housing stock.
evidence: 7 indoor air quality complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (195% increase, z-score: 4.16)
Heat/hot water remains chronic crisis: 2,151 complaints over 90 days (2nd highest category)
Potential correlation with 322 alteration permits filed—may indicate inadequate HVAC in renovation projects or disruptive construction affecting air quality
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality spikes with heat/hot water complaints: are landlords leaving units unheated/improperly ventilated?
Interview residents: are complaints tied to specific buildings or a district-wide issue? Check for violations/DOB complaints at complaint addresses
